title: Faith as essence vs existence — weak faith often lacks absolute certainty
source_text: XVII. Hic vero ante omnia notandum est, fidem duobus modis considerari posse. Vel secundum essentiam, ut loquuntur Philosophi, id est, qualis esse potest, & debet natura sua, & secundum perfectiones quae illi ex suo genere debentur, & ratione habita objecti quod respicit. Vel secundum existentiam, id est, qualis actu est in hoc aut illo subjecto. Si fides consideretur hoc posteriore modo, manifestum est ei, saltem semper, non competere certitudinem illam summam & absolutam. In multis enim fides infirma est, & tentationibus variis succutitur, ac perpetuam habet cum dubitatione & diffidentia luctam. Qualis erat fides illius qui Domino Jesu Christo dicebat, Credo Domine, succurre incredulitati meae. Et discipulorum, quos Christus vocat ὀλιγοπίστους, & qui propterea illi quoque dicebant, Adauge nobis fidem.
pass_a_gloss: But here before all it is to be noted that faith can be considered in two ways. Either according to essence, as the Philosophers speak — that is, such as it can be and ought to be by its nature, and according to the perfections owed to it from its own kind, regard being had to the object it looks to. Or according to existence — that is, such as it actually is in this or that subject. If faith is considered in this latter way, it is plain that to it, at least not always, that highest and absolute certainty does not belong. For in many faith is weak, and is shaken by various temptations, and has a perpetual struggle with doubt and distrust. Such was the faith of him who said to the Lord Jesus Christ, I believe, Lord; help my unbelief. And of the disciples, whom Christ calls of little faith, and who therefore also said to Him, Increase our faith.
pass_b_english: Faith two ways: essence (what it can/ought to be) vs existence (as it actually is in someone).
As existent: highest absolute certainty does not always belong.
Weak faith wrestles doubt — Mark 9:24; disciples ὀλιγόπιστοι; Luke 17:5 Increase our faith.
